subject.title: fix(ci): bound openclaw-npm-release git fetch operations with timeout

question: Should every npm-release fetch fail after 120 seconds with a 10-second termination grace period, including valid but unusually slow release-network operations?
rationale: The code correctly implements the proposed bound, but choosing an acceptable release-network deadline is an operational risk decision owned by the release team rather than something automated review can infer.

options.title: Approve after proof
options.body: Keep the proposed deadline, require inspectable six-path stall evidence, and then land with release-owner approval.

options.title: Use a longer deadline
options.body: Preserve the per-command timeout design but increase the initial deadline to the release team's accepted worst-case fetch budget.

options.title: Decline the bound
options.body: Keep current fetch behavior and accept that a stalled transport may occupy the release runner until the broader job timeout.

recommendation.title: Approve after proof
recommendation.body: Keep the proposed deadline, require inspectable six-path stall evidence, and then land with release-owner approval.

likelyOwner.reason: CODEOWNERS assigns this workflow and its release-path checks directly to that team.
